validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The two wiki-cited news links are real leads, not generic mentions -- both cover a Sept-26 pipeline rupture near Boryspil (railway cable-laying damage) and NAME the pipeline explicitly. jkg-portal.com.ua (Ukraine Komunalna): 'Магистральный газопровод «Шебелинка-Полтава-Київ» построен в 1960 г., общая длина 454,7 км, диаметр 700 мм' (built 1960, total length 454.7 km, diameter 700 mm). censor.net, same incident, independent outlet: '...был поврежден подземный магистральный газопровод Шебелинка-Полтава-Киев (диаметр 720 мм давление 40 атм)' (diameter 720 mm, pressure 40 atm), dated to 26 Sept 2011 in the article text. Both are independent Ukrainian news origins (different publishers, different wording), neither traces to GEM/gem.wiki. A THIRD independent origin: Ukrtransgaz's own official corporate history timeline (utg.ua, direct fetch 403s -- accessed via Wayback) records under year 1961: 'Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Шебелинка - Полтава - Київ, який перетнув центральну частину Дніпровсько-Донецької западини' (commissioned the trunk gas pipeline Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv, which crossed the central Dnieper-Donets depression). Three independent sources, none GEM-derived, all naming this specific pipeline -- existence is solid, tier=high. The wiki's other two citations (tsoua.com key-facts, a LinkedIn company page) are generic GTS-operator pages that do NOT name this pipeline; they are not usable as pipeline-specific support (noted, not relied on for existence). CLASSIFICATION: all three independent sources call it a 'магистральный/магістральний газопровід' (trunk gas transmission pipeline), consistent with GEM's classification -- not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the roster's 'Dikanka family' (P1453 Efremovka-Dikanka(/Dolyna)-Kiev, P1454 Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kiev, P1460 Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Krivyi Rih): the same Ukrtransgaz history timeline independently documents these as SEPARATE, sequentially-built trunk lines, not the same pipe under different names -- 1961 Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv (this row); 1968 construction start / 1970 commissioning of Efremovka-Dolyna-Kyiv (matches P1453's family, note the timeline's route word is 'Долина' not 'Диканька' for the 1970 commissioning entry, a P1453-scoped detail flagged here only for the next pass); 1973 commissioning of Shebelinka-Диканька(Dikanka)-Kyiv (matches P1454 exactly, confirming P1454 as a real, later, separate expansion parallel to this row -- both lines feed Kyiv from Shebelinka via different routes/years); 1964 commissioning of a Poltava-Kremenchuk line (relevant to P1460's family, not resolved here). P1452 is NOT a duplicate of any of these -- it is the earliest (1960/61) of the Shebelinka-to-Kyiv corridor lines and has its own distinct history-book entry. SPEC (StartYear): GEM's StartYear1=1960 matches jkg-portal's 'построен в 1960 г.' exactly (construction-completion year). Ukrtransgaz's own history page separately lists 1961 as the formal 'введено в експлуатацію' (commissioned/put into operation) year for the same pipeline -- a plausible construction-vs-commissioning distinction, not a contradiction of GEM's stored value. Not flagged as a concern; GEM's value is directly corroborated.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat Diameter=720mm as settled. Two independent Ukrainian outlets reporting on the SAME September 2011 Boryspil rupture disagree: censor.net states 720 mm (matches GEM's stored value); jkg-portal.com.ua, covering the identical incident, states 700 mm. Flag for a further pass -- ideally against a TSOU/ENTSOG technical document rather than incident news.
validity.researcher_notes: Both articles describe the same rupture event (same date, same location near Boryspil, same cause -- unauthorized cable-laying by a construction firm, same pipeline name) yet give different diameters: censor.net '(диаметр 720 мм давление 40 атм)' vs jkg-portal 'диаметр 700 мм'. Since GEM's stored value (720mm) coincidentally matches one of the two disagreeing sources, this is NOT independently corroborated -- it is a live conflict between the two only independent sources found. A material disagreement on diameter (700 vs 720mm) that must not be silently passed through as confirmed.

fills.researcher_notes: jkg-portal.com.ua (2011 rupture-repair article, independent Ukrainian outlet, unrelated to GEM) states the pipeline's 'общая длина 454,7 км' -- an exact match to GEM's stored 454.70 km. Single explicit numeric source found (tier=medium); no second independent source with a length figure located.

jkg-portal.com.ua states 'построен в 1960 г.' matching GEM's StartYear1=1960 exactly. Ukrtransgaz's own official history page separately dates formal commissioning ('введено в експлуатацію') to 1961 for the same pipeline -- a plausible construction-vs-commissioning distinction, not treated as a conflict (see validity note).

Both 2011 articles document the pipeline actively carrying gas at pressure (40 atm per censor.net) at the time of the rupture, with supply restored within a day -- direct evidence of active service. No post-2011 status source located, but nothing found suggests decommissioning, and per country background Ukraine's domestic GTS continues operating despite the Jan-2025 halt of Russian transit (transit cessation is not evidence about this specific line's in-service status). Tier=medium given the dated (2011) sourcing.
Both independent sources explicitly call it a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline) supplying settlements' 'газоснабжение' (gas supply); trivially confirms Fuel=Gas.

Both independent sources name the pipeline 'Шебелинка-Полтава-Киев/Київ' and locate the rupture near Boryspil, on the Kyiv Oblast side of the corridor, consistent with a Shebelinka(Kharkiv Oblast)->Kyiv route via Poltava. Confirms Start=Shebelinka, End=Kiev, both Ukraine.

Single-source (tier=medium) since it is the operator's own statement about itself, not a third-party confirmation, but it is authoritative for the current legal/organizational fact.

summary: Existence/classification confirmed high-tier via 3 independent sources (2 Ukrainian news outlets on a named 2011 rupture near Boryspil + Ukrtransgaz's own 1961 corporate-history entry); confirmed NOT a duplicate of the Dikanka-family rows (P1453/P1454/P1460), which the same history timeline documents as separate, later, sequentially-built lines. Length (454.70km) and StartYear1 (1960) both matched exactly by an independent source; Owner (Gas TSO of Ukraine) confirmed via the operator's own key-facts page. One real spec concern staged: Diameter (720mm) is contested -- two independent outlets covering the identical incident disagree (700mm vs 720mm), left UNRESOLVED rather than silently confirmed.
